Definition: from G1722 and γυῖον (a limb); pledged (as if articulated by a member), i.e. a bondsman:--surety.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus was made a surety of a better testament in Hebrews 7:22 — He stands as the guarantee of the new covenant, the one who answers for it with His own life.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a surety is only as good as his ability to pay, and Jesus paid in full, which is why the better covenant can never fail.
